AI is able to produce entirely new outputs and discover previously unknown mathematic solutions. I think you suffer from the same misconception that the chess players of the 1980's suffered from ; you think the human mind is absolutely singular in its nature and that it cannot ever be emulated by machines. And you are wrong. Ask yourself this : if human reasonning is simply neurons being fired in our brain and interacting with our memory, then why can't a neural network with petabytes of memory reason? You talk about training but it is exactly what human brains do. Humans can't read or write until they are taught to do so, we have very little inate knowledge, except perhaps the knowledge of breathing and looking around. All the rest (even hand movements) is being learned through months of experimentation at best, or it is straight up taught to us. In that sense we are no different than the AI.
"But AI can't generate new ideas, it only uses prefed concepts to reach new conclusion" that's also exactly how we work. Mathematicians and philosophers base their entire thesis on knowledge previously developed. No artists has ever drawn a face or a hand without seeing and training on thousands and thousands of faces and arms. Everything we do is based on training and building new blocks on existing knowledge

62887046
>>62886734
I don't think AI actually does create anything new, but that's complicated by the fact that human invention covers so much, there is little left that is "new". Consider: from 1900 to 2000, there was an explosion and proliferation of new technologies and discoveries. We went from telegraphcs to fiber optic cables. But the progress has slowed with every decade, and microwaves today are little changed from microwaves 20 years ago. They are still the same basic shit, with more bells and whistles attached.

Ai does not need to make "new" stuff to be useful; it's excellent and reorganizing and collating the vast corpus of human invention into useful fabrications. It's also capable of doing design work that is radically alien and "natural", in the sense that it works well but engineers probably wouldn't have designed it (usually aesthetic principles dominate).

An AI may not invent the factory; it can retool and redesign the human factory to be 100x more productive and efficient. And eventually it can do the labor too; there is nothing special about labor. Anything a human can do can be replicated by a robot of sufficient complexity.

That is the future for AI.
